summary: What a portfolio decided about each thing it holds: its priority, and whether to invest in it, hold it or stop it.
example: This season: invest in the Quality Improvement Programme first; hold the member app until its pilot reports.
definition: The decisions a portfolio has made at its latest review, one for each project, programme or portfolio it holds: a priority, a decision (invest: fund it and let it go on; hold: keep it, but commit nothing more until the next review; stop: end it and release what it holds), the reason and the date. Kept in a file of its own beside the portfolio, as a KPI's readings are, because decisions change at every review while the portfolio's definition does not (TAXONOMY.md D8, D32).

/spec/portfolio.guide: The portfolio these decisions belong to.

/metadata/name.guide: A name for this set of decisions, usually the review it came from.

/spec/decisions.guide: One row for each thing the portfolio holds, and nothing else.

/spec/decisions/-/kind.guide: Whether the decision is about a project, a programme or a portfolio.

/spec/decisions/-/id.guide: The project, programme or portfolio decided on. It names this portfolio itself.

/spec/decisions/-/priority.guide: Its rank: 1 is first. Two things may share a rank.

/spec/decisions/-/reason.guide: Why, in a sentence a reader would accept.
good: Moves the pass rate most for the least spend this season.

poor.why: Says nothing a reader can check: say what it advances, or what has to change first.
